Four Nb–16Si–18Ti– xB( x = 0, 1, 2, 3) alloys were prepared by arc melting in a water-cooled copper crucible under an argon atmosphere. The alloys were made of high-purity Nb (99.9%), Si (99.9%), sponge titanium (99.6%) and TiB2 powder. Each ingot was remelted five times to ensure compositional homogeneity.

The addition of B promotes the formation of a-Nb5Si3 phase and suppresses the formation of Nb3Si phase. B addition also tends Nb–16Si–18Ti alloy to form the hypereutectic structures.

It can be interpreted as that Ostwald ripening happens in the investigated alloys [17] after heat treatment, and that is to say, large particles grow at the expense of small ones by the growth from small to large particles.

The compression strength is vastly affected by grain size and morphology of silicide phases due to that the silicide phases are brittle phases and the bulk silicide phases easily form crack, which will deteriorate room temperature compression strength [27].
